title: Good for bare floors and outdoor carpets; not good for pet hair or those with pile carpets
text:
Good for bare floors and outdoor carpets; not good for pet hair or those with pile carpets. I wanted a canister vacuum as a backup to an old Kenmore canister vacuum I own. After trying this vacuum, I feel my old Kenmore Progressive 360 Swivel TrueHEPA is far superior (even though it's breaking apart).

Below are the PROS and CONS of this Dyson:

PROS

Installation was easy and the pictures provided in the manual were easy to understand for dis-assembly of certain parts (like the canister).

The cord is sufficiently long. I measured it twice and it is around 21-1/2 to 22 feet.

The maneuverability of the vacuum is great and so is the turning radius.

When vacuuming floors, the beater bar (brush bar) can be turned off by toggling the button on the handle.

The cord is retractable with the press of a button.

The canister is extremely easy to release and empty and hair didn't get caught in the cylinder like other bagless vacuums I have tried. Even though this is not a HEPA vacuum, I did not sneeze like I usually do when emptying other bagless vacuums.

Once the canister is removed from the base, the filter is easy to remove by lifting straight up and out. It is also easy to re-seat the canister to the base.

The tool caddy fits securely around the extension arm and the two tools sit snugly in that holder even while vacuuming. The tools are also easy to use. The crevice tool has a retractable brush; so it's a 2-in-1 tool. There's also what I would call the narrow floor tool. I did not see a name for it in the book.

The vacuum has great suction. Because the suction is so great, even with the release valve that reduces suction, I still had to use the brush tool provided to vacuum a pet bed successfully because the beater bar wanted to suck in the entire bed.

The beater bar turns easily and is small enough to fit between the legs of some of my furniture which is very nice.

The vacuum moves easily along bare floors and works great for that.

The vacuum is relatively quiet compared to some other vacuums I've used before.

The wand extends with the push of a button. I found it comfortable to vacuum when the wand was fully extended. I'm 5 feet 5 inches so I would suspect someone over 6 feet might feel the extension is not long enough; although for me it was perfect and I could have even collapsed it a bit.

The filter is washable. Dyson recommends it be washed with cold water on a monthly basis. It must be left to dry 24 hours before the next use.

The orange color is very nice and with the purplish blue trim of the filter and silver gray color of the base and hoses, it is an attractive vacuum.

A 5-year warranty is provided for parts and labor

CONS

Dyson recommends the filter be washed with cold water on a monthly basis and it must be left to air dry 24 hours before the next use. I believe the washing recommendations should be based on use. For instance, saying the filter should be washed after 2-3 hours of continuous or non-continuous use is better than a flat schedule because perhaps a user only vacuums once a month or once every two months.

The power button is located on the canister and not on the handle. This is a negative for me because I had to keep bending down and walking over to the canister to shut the unit on and off whenever I needed.

The biggest negative for me is that the beater bar gets clogged easily with hair and I found it almost impossible to remove the bar as shown. Using a tool like a screwdriver (or even a letter opener handle) damaged the plastic dome covering the beater bar. They did not say with what to remove the cover. I have four long-haired cats and I had to clean the beater bar at least once before I finished vacuuming because it kept getting tangled with all the hair that was picked up. Even though you couldn't see the hair on the carpet, the Dyson was exceptional in pulling whatever hair there was from the carpet. I don't have this problem with my Kenmore because the beater bar bristles are tiny and don't seem to hold onto the hair like this vacuum does. From now on I will clean the bar by pulling the hair out instead of removing the entire bar as recommended. It was also difficult to lock the bar in place simply because the plastic cover did not provide any turning leverage. This was the only part of the vacuum that I found difficult to lock and unlock.

The other big negative was that I have somewhat low-pile carpet, yet the suction was so great it was hard to move the vacuum over the carpet unless I opened the "suction trigger release" on the handle to reduce the airflow. I found that I had to use this release continuously. However, I did not have to use it on the outdoor carpet on my balcony which is low pile carpet that is almost like a bare floor.

The other negative was the comment in the manual that says "fine dirt such as flour should only be vacuumed in small quantities." That means I cannot use carpet powder with this vacuum. I like to put down carpet powder to give my house a flowery smell. The powder I put down adds up to almost an entire box worth for my condo. However, with this vacuum I really should not do that because it would clog the filter.

In summary, this Dyson has some great qualities such as good maneuverability, easy and light to carry, great on bare floors, and good suction. However, I feel that for those with pets or carpet in their house (unless it's outdoor carpet), would not find this vacuum a good buy. I also feel at the current price of $399, it is too expensive because of the CONS even though I'm impressed with its great qualities. In fact, I really would love this vacuum if I did not have carpet. Depending on the a person's circumstances I can see some loving this vacuum, other's liking it, most seeing it as okay, and some might even hate it. Based on the PROS and CONS above, it's just okay for my purposes.

UPDATE May 25, 2014 - I felt that my boyfriend would love this vacuum because he has a no pile carpet in one room and wood floors in the rest of his apartment. Since it's also compact and has excellent maneuverability (features I love), he would love that too. Today, I had him try this vacuum at his place and he LOVES it and rates it 5 stars just as I expected. Therefore, if I had the same situation in my house, I would have rated this 5 stars as well. Since it does not work for my purposes, I rated it 3 stars. This vacuum is for those who either don't mind releasing the airflow through the handle pull or for those who don't have pile carpet and want it mostly for hard wood or bare floors.

Whole-machine HEPA filtration traps allergens and bacteria inside the machine
